verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. 02.02.03:20 does say the Musician's card-confirming tap 'is the attestation (`02.04.01`)', and 02.02.03:97 does say confirmed claims become 'session-captured + attested credits'. Verification found the contradiction is stronger than the finding claims: 02.02.03:171 (DT-05) states the model as a deliberate design conclusion, not a slip — 'Every contributor's tap attests their *own* row. Nobody's tap attests "produced by X"' — and the whole D-08 reciprocal-line fix is derived from it. Against that, 02.04.01:251 (D-11) excludes the credited party from the addressable set, 02.04.01:154 says their own row shows 'waiting on others', **never a self-confirm control**, and 02.04.02:52/204 gate rungs 5 and 6 on an attester who is 'neither the asserter nor the credited party'. Not tracked anywhere: no Open Question, no PENDING marker, no CX reconciliation. The domain CX-02 (credits-attribution-cx.md:17) restates 02.02.03's side ('The in-room tap at close *is* the attestation'), and the sub-domain CX (02.02-session-capture-cx.md:67) offers a third model ('the corroborating value comes from the *set*') that satisfies neither rung gate. Two normative statements that cannot both hold, on the product's stated wedge: a self-confirm control either exists on the close-prompt card or is forbidden.

Quotes verified verbatim at 02.01.01:90-91 and :138. The divergence is real — a self-confirmation cannot reach rung 6 under 02.04.02:53 and :204 — but downgraded from blocking because this is the same root divergence as #001 expressed in a non-owning file, and the resolution path is one citation hop. 02.01.01:91 cites `02.04.02` for the tier claim; following that citation lands on the rung table (02.04.02:44-53) and D-08 (02.04.02:204), which govern tier derivation and contradict the 'highest tier there is' claim. 02.01.01 is the ledger feature and does not own the tier model, so an implementer resolves to 02.04.02. What remains genuinely wrong and unflagged is the prose itself, which will read as authoritative to anyone who does not follow the reference. Fix follows automatically from whichever way #001 is ratified.

The quotes exist but the claim misreads them. 02.01.02 does NOT treat a party-set control as globally suppressed — its own definition at 02.01.02:20 is exactly the Unlisted semantic: 'sets per-credit visibility via `02.01.05` (**Private hides a line from the page without deleting the record**)'. Every other cited line is scoped to that party's discography page, which is the entire subject of 02.01.02: the Fan line (:23), viewer-relative counts (:45), the suppressed-empty state (:98) and the restrictive-propagation edge case (:81) all describe one page's contents, not the work ledger or co-contributor pages. Nothing in 02.01.02 says an Unlisted credit leaves the work's ledger or the graph. 02.01.05 itself confirms the split and assigns it: 02.01.05:253 — 'Axis B (Unlisted) is a property **this page renders and only this page**'. The 404 rule (02.01.02:156, :80) traces its stated authority to `02.01.05` D-04, which is the embargo leak rule, and 02.01.05:23 independently states the 404 for embargoed credits. What actually survives is stale vocabulary — 02.01.02 uses the superseded label 'Private' where 02.01.05 D-06 renamed it 'Unlisted' — which is terminology hygiene, not a forced product invention.
verdicts.evidence: 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.02-public-discography.md:20 ('hides a line from the page without deleting the record'); 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:253 ('a property this page renders and only this page'), :23, :46

verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim at 02.01.02:69, :114, :154 and 02.01.05:50, :231. The contradiction is real and I tested the obvious escape: whether the named party has some other unilateral control that would make the remedy claim true. They do not. 02.01.05:39/:181/:203 make Confidential require 'the assent of both the credited party and the work's ledger owner', and 02.01.05:20 states the Musician 'Cannot ... remove themselves from a work's ledger'. So the only unilateral control is Unlisted, and 02.01.05:50 says in terms that a party using it 'will find their name on the work's public ledger and on four co-contributors' pages'. 02.03.03:114-119 Q-04 confirms the shape of the hole for the adjacent claimant case and notes 02.01.01 D-11 refuses a claimant-side suppression control. Downgraded from blocking: D-06's rule (no public contested marker) is unambiguous and 02.01.05 D-06 mandates the honest UI copy, so nothing is invented at build time. What is defective is a load-bearing rejected-alternative rationale resting on a remedy the owning feature says does not work, plus the edge-case row at :69 that instructs a user-facing flow to promise an effect it cannot deliver.

Quotes verified, but the invention the finding claims is forced is answered in four independent places, all normative and all agreeing. 02.10:122 (D-04) 'You disclose your own contribution only'; 02.10:71 edge case 'Producer discloses AI on someone else's contribution | **Not permitted**'; credits-attribution-cx.md:260 (CX-14) makes it a locked per-field ownership split — 'the Producer owns the attribution on the row, and the *named contributor* owns its AI-disclosure axis ... must not be collapsible by whoever holds the row'; and 02.02.02:109 refuses the write at the capture surface. No implementer builds a cross-party AI write against four converging refusals including a dedicated CX entry authored to lock exactly this. The second half — 'what is a session-level disclosure' — is self-answering rather than open: 02.10:33-42 binds a disclosure to a contribution and no session-scoped entity, field, scope value or state exists anywhere in the file, so there is nothing to build. The Access column reading 'Full' (02.10:19, mirrored at credits-attribution-index.md:85) is the coarse legend defined at credits-attribution-index.md:72 and is used unqualified for many roles; it is loose Role Lens prose against a fully specified contribution-scoped model, not a competing permission grant.

Quotes verified verbatim. 02.04-attestation-credit-confidence-cx.md:77 does say 'the dispute holds the tier (`02.04.02` states), so the retraction's effect **must queue** rather than apply', and 02.04.02:206 (D-10), :123 and :144 say the opposite in three places — 'A contest neither moves nor freezes the rung', 'no freeze', 'Rung continues to derive normally'. Not tracked: no marker on the CX line, no Open Question covering it, and 02.04.03 (the retraction feature) contains no queue-during-dispute rule at all. Downgraded from blocking because the resolution is discoverable in one hop and lands decisively: the CX line cites 02.04.02's States table as its authority, that table says the opposite, and 02.04.02 is the owning feature for rung derivation — so a competent implementer resolves against the CX, not for it. The CX synthesis line is stale relative to the deepened 02.04.02 and needs correcting, but it does not force a product invention.

Quotes verified, but the only decidable question the finding raises is explicitly settled, and settled against interval scoping. 02.01.05:115 (DT-13, and the full rejection at :232) states: 'Explicitly rejected: scoping a participant's visibility to the intervals they attended ... Participant status is per session, binary. **The temporality of the roll matters for *attribution*; it does not matter for *confidentiality*.**' That sentence is the reconciliation — it names both rules and assigns each its object. 02.02.01 D-09 governs roll visibility (working data, an attribution surface); 02.01.05 governs credit confidentiality. Both are implementable exactly as written and neither constrains the other, so two implementers converge. What survives is that D-09's rationale clause at 02.02.01:216/:145 overstates the protection it buys — the async contributor learns the personnel from the embargoed credits minutes later at commit — which is a rationale defect, not an ambiguity, and the file it would be corrected against has already anticipated and answered the question.
verdicts.evidence: 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:115, :232 ('The temporality of the roll matters for attribution; it does not matter for confidentiality') vs 02.02-session-capture/02.02.01-session-roll-call.md:145, :216

verdicts.reason: Quotes verified, but the finding stops one clause short of the resolution. 02.02.03:185 does not merely flag the stale chain — it states the correction inline: 'CX-02 records "wrap → reconcile → prompt → confirmations", which is the sequential model DT-04 rejects. **The corrected chain is "wrap → {contributor asks ∥ reconciliation} → confirmations", with the two halves running concurrently.**' Nothing is left to invent; the replacement text is authored, and it is reinforced by 02.02.03:206 (D-05), :96 Happy Path 3 ('Within 5 s, both halves fire at once ... Neither waits for the other'), and by the sub-domain index itself, which already carries the corrected model — 02.02-session-capture-index.md:49 quotes D-05 verbatim as the resolution of its Q-03. So the sub-domain's own index is current even though one synthesis line in its CX file is not. The residue is a stale sentence in a sibling artifact whose correct value is written down twice in the same sub-domain — editorial, not a divergence. The Step-6-has-run observation is fair but does not change that, since the fix does not depend on a stage running.

02.08:50 is quoted correctly, but one supporting citation is misattributed — 'Scope (participant vs catalog) is the permission...' is at credits-attribution-cx.md:207, not 02.01.05:207. More importantly the scope rule is stated five times, including nine lines below the Happy Path in the same file: 02.08:59 'participant-scoped export may include them'; 02.01.05:163 resolves it in full ('a participant may export the embargoed credits of sessions they participated in ... A non-participant-scoped export (a Producer's whole catalog, a room's discography) excludes'); 02.01.05:253; credits-attribution-cx.md:25 and :200, the last recording it as already-resolved ('Step 5 resolved the pending scope question'). The two predicates also do not actually select different sets in any case the corpus specifies: 02.01.05:163's participant-scoped export is the participant exporting for themselves, so exporter, scope and recipient coincide; the catalog case excludes under both readings. 02.01.05 D-09's guarantee is therefore not broken. Loose Happy Path wording against five converging statements — no implementer diverges.

The marker exists verbatim at 02.02.04:49 and the observation that it names no owner is correct. But it sits in the **User Sees** column only — the What Happens column already decides the substance in full ('Topology is the only defence (`02.04.04`), not evidence strength — and that defence is score-only ... **Accepted cost, stated plainly**: a fully corroborated fiction keeps its top rung indefinitely'). What the user sees in that scenario is likewise decided elsewhere, and decided as 'nothing': 02.04.02:147 (Demoted (score) state) — 'The rung does not move (D-19) ... **Silent, and now silent by construction rather than by policy: there is no visible label to change**'; 02.01.02:78 states the same row's user-visible outcome outright — '**Nothing, to anyone, ever.** No label change, no notification, no reordering of this page'; 02.04.04 D-02 forbids surfacing it as an oracle. The file's three Open Questions do not cover it because there is nothing left to decide. Stale tracking on a cell whose answer is written down three times.

The marker exists verbatim at 02.03.03:69 and carries no owner. But all three named downstream effects are already routed by a general, repeatedly-stated domain boundary. Royalty registration: 02.04.02:125 — 'Domain 02 supplies rung-at-time-T (DT-16) ... **it does not unwind anything**'; 02.04.03:91 (Q-03) is resolved with the ownership cited to `ideation-cx.md` item 20 — '10 owns registration ... the unwind and its cost are domain 10's to specify'; 02.04.04:83 states the same boundary from the demotion side, explicitly as 'same shape as `02.04.03` Q-03'. Reputation: routed out of domain 02 entirely by domain D-07 (02.04.02:210, D-14 'No party-level aggregate tier'). Traversal edges: derived from the credit graph at query (02.01.03), so they re-derive rather than unwind. The finding's own comparator is the answer — 02.04.03 Q-03 is not a differently-handled sibling but the general rule this case falls under. The residual defect is that 02.03.03:69 asserts effects 'must unwind' without citing the boundary that says domain 02 does not unwind them; that is a missing cross-reference, not an open decision.
